stem: If \(-4 < 2 - 3x \le 11\), what is the least possible value of \(x\)?
solution: Divide by \(-3\) and reverse both signs: \(2 > x \ge -3\), that is, \(-3 \le x < 2\).
The least possible value of \(x\) is \(-3\). Check: \(2 - 3(-3) = 11\).
verify:
x = symbols('x')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(-4 < 2 - 3*x, x, relational=False).intersect(solve_univariate_inequality(2 - 3*x <= 11, x, relational=False))
assert s == Interval.Ropen(-3, 2)
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [s.inf]
